thread:
maria: Heads up - nightly archive job flagged ~120 S3 objects uploaded without the expected sse-cmk metadata/tag. Some downstream restores failed with AccessDenied from KMS. Anyone oncall?
encops-bot: Alert: 5632104321 - s3:PutObject missing encryption metadata detected (CI archive-batcher). See /alerts/5632104321
sam: oncall here. can you paste the error from the restore path? AccessDenied from KMS or 403 from S3?
maria: KMS AccessDenied during decrypt in restore lambda. error snippet: `AccessDeniedException: Not authorized to use KMS key arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd-...` - happens intermittently across objects.
alice: first suspicion: uploader service account recently had IAM role changes last night. can we check who assumed the uploader role during the window? cloudtrail quick query:
``
lookup-events --lookup-attributes AttributeKey=EventName,AttributeValue=PutObject --start-time "2026-03-19T00:00:00Z" --end-time "2026-03-19T06:00:00Z"
```
jon: i skimmed the deploys - there was a credential refresh PR (repo: infra/s3-uploader, PR 482) merged ~01:12 UTC. it changed how metadata headers are set (switched to a multipart helper).
maria: if the uploader stopped attaching x-amz-meta-sse-cmk-tag (or our internal tag) then later restore flow can't map to CMK grants. this smells like metadata propagation bug + KMS grant mismatch.
tony: also check ephemeral KMS grants TTL. if uploader was granted a short-lived grant and then expired, but objects were uploaded with a key alias we don't map, restore will fail. cloudtrail KMS events query helps:
``
-- filter: KMS ReEncrypt/GenerateDataKey events where userIdentity = uploader-sa
```
sam: can we confirm whether objects themselves are encrypted server-side (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS), or were uploaded unencrypted? head-object output:
``
aws s3api head-object --bucket redwood-archives --key archives/2026/03/19/0001.tar.gz
# Response: { "ServerSideEncryption":"aws:kms", "SSEKMSKeyId":"arn:aws:kms:...:key/abcd-...", "Metadata":{} }
```
alice: that response is the problem - Metadata is empty (we expect `x-amz-meta-encops-tag: escrow-v2`). uploader helper used to set that, new helper didn't. PR 482 change log shows header omission.
maria: mitigation plan:
- block the new uploader deploy (rollback PR 482) - jordan can you coordinate? 
- add temporary fallback in restore lambda: if metadata missing, map by bucket+prefix -> try known CMK aliases (log heavily) 
- run canary restores for 10 objects before unblocking traffic
- audit grant TTLs and re-grant as needed

jordan: rolling PR 482 back now, will route to rollback pipeline. estimated 10m. will also tag the 120 affected objects with `x-amz-meta-encops-tag: escrow-v2` using a bulk script once we confirm canonical key mapping.
tony: for bulk tagging, please don't re-upload - use copy-object with metadata replace. example:
``
aws s3 cp s3://redwood-archives/obj s3://redwood-archives/obj --metadata-add x-amz-meta-encops-tag=escrow-v2 --metadata-directive REPLACE
```
sam: make sure the copy operation uses the same SSE-KMS key or you'll hit KMS decrypt/re-encrypt; run in a region with KMS access.
alice: i'll open an audit ticket to track: who assumed uploader-SA during the window, which KMS grants were issued, and which restores failed. add timeline (deploy, uploader-role-change, failures).
encops-bot: Playbook: encops/s3-missing-meta - steps: rollback uploader, tag affected objects, run canary restores, re-evaluate KMS grant policies. Link: /playbooks/encops-s3-missing-meta
maria: one more ask - security: please snapshot CloudTrail logs for the 01:00-02:00 UTC window and mark as evidence. we may need this for compliance review.
jordan: rollback succeeded. I'll start tagging script in dry-run, will post results + counts here.
tony: i'll run the KMS grant audit and post anomalies. will check for grants that were issued with `RetireOn` < now.
sam: after canaries succeed, we should schedule a postmortem and a stricter pre-deploy test that verifies metadata headers end-to-end for archive uploads.
maria: agreed. thanks all. tagging numbers: initial dry-run found 118 objects missing meta; will report after actual run. :thumbsup:
